name: Je'iel (A descendant of Adonikam who went up from Babylon with Ezra)
title: A descendant of Adonikam who returned from exile
summary: Je'iel was a descendant of Adonikam among the last to go up from Babylon to Jerusalem with Ezra. He is mentioned in the book of Ezra as part of the second wave of returning exiles during the reign of King Artaxerxes. His return was part of God's plan to rebuild the Jewish community in Judah.

keyEvents.title: Listed among those who returned
keyEvents.description: Je'iel is mentioned as one of the last descendants of Adonikam to go up from Babylon to Jerusalem with Ezra.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's caravan gathers at the Ahava River
keyEvents.description: Ezra gathered the returnees by the river that flows to Ahava, where they prepared for the journey to Jerusalem. Je'iel was among those who gathered there.

keyEvents.title: Fasting and prayer before departure
keyEvents.description: Ezra proclaimed a fast at the Ahava River to seek God's protection on the dangerous journey to Jerusalem, which Je'iel participated in as part of the caravan.

keyEvents.title: The safe arrival in Jerusalem
keyEvents.description: After God's protection on the journey, the caravan arrived safely in Jerusalem, where they rested for three days before handing over the temple gifts.

keyEvents.title: The descendants of Adonikam in the first return
keyEvents.description: Adonikam's descendants are also mentioned among those who returned earlier with Zerubbabel, showing the family's long-standing connection to the return.
